subject: Private deployment containment lanes & rollback choreography — maintenance window proposal
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Paul Simmons <paul.simmons@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Aug 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment containment lanes & rollback choreography — maintenance window proposal

Hi Paul —

Per our recent check-ins, we’re planning a short maintenance window for your private VPC deployment to apply a critical runtime patch and related kernel updates. I want to propose a focused plan that minimizes risk and gives us a clean escape hatch if anything looks off. High-level details below: 

- Proposed window: Thu 2025-08-14 01:00–03:00 UTC (local evening for your ops). Please confirm blackout constraints.
- Scope: runtime patch, kernel-level runtime libs, model-serving quantization hotfix. No schema or data migration expected.
- Version pin behavior: we will pin the fleet to current stable on controller and then roll a canary (10% nodes) with KV cache priming. If canary passes, we proceed in 25% waves.
- Containment lanes: network cordon per-rack (BGP refresh + interface drain), client traffic routed to warm fallback variant (same model family, lower perf profile) for requests that exceed latency SLO during the window.
- Telemetry & gating: we’ll watch 95th/99th latency, error-rate, token error traces, and request-level traces. If latency >200ms above baseline or error-rate >1% for 5m on canary, we abort to rollback.
- Rollback choreography: controller triggers automated unpin and sequence-reverse rollout; KV caches will be invalidated then gracefully rebuilt. We’ll also stash pre-upgrade node snapshots for fast redeploy (restore time target 8–12 min per node).
- Audit & compliance: we’ll capture operation logs and a signed runbook snapshot for your records.

Attached are the draft runbook and the pin/unpin checklist. Please review and flag any network constraints or audit requirements we should include (e.g., mandated log retention window). Also confirm the proposed window or suggest alternatives.

Thanks —
Stephanie Nguyen
Sr. Platform PM, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: maintenance_runbook_v1.pdf (runbook stub), pin-unpin-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Paul Simmons <paul.simmons@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Aug 2025 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment containment lanes & rollback choreography — maintenance window proposal

Stephanie —

Thanks for the clear plan. A couple of internal asks before we lock the window: 

1) BGP/route refresh: add an explicit step to perform a BGP route refresh and wait for adjacency stabilization before traffic cutover. Note the expected convergence time and include a readout gate.
2) Metrics retention snapshot: export 1h pre-upgrade aggregated histograms for 50/90/95/99 percentiles and attach to the runbook; we should persist those with the audit bundle.
3) Inter-region fallbacks: confirm that the warm fallback variant will not cross regions (we should avoid cross-region egress unless the customer explicitly okays it).

I’ve annotated the runbook with comments — will send a slim patch.

–Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Private Ops Engineering
Redwood Inference

Stephanie, Karthik —

Thanks for the detailed plan and the attachments. A few quick items from Acme: 

- The proposed window on Thu 01:00–03:00 UTC works for our on-call team. No blackout conflicts.
- Please confirm the SLA for rollback: our compliance team wants an RTO target if we hit rollback that we can use in internal reporting. Your note of 8–12 min per node is helpful — can you provide a conservative end-to-end RTO estimate for our fleet size (we’re currently at ~48 serving nodes pinned)?
- Audit evidence: we require signed runbook snapshots and operation logs retained for 90 days. Will you provide the runbook snapshot plus the orchestration event log?

Also: will the fallback variant reduce feature parity (e.g., function/tool-calling hooks) or is it a like-for-like behavioral fallback with just lower perf?

Appreciate the careful approach — please send the estimated RTO and confirm log retention and fallback behavior.

Best,
Paul Simmons
SRE Manager
Acme Analytics

Subject: Re: Private deployment containment lanes & rollback choreography — maintenance window proposal

Paul —

Great, thanks for the quick confirmation and the questions. Short answers below, followed by the action items we’ll take before the window.

- Conservative RTO estimate: with 48 nodes we ballpark an end-to-end rollback RTO of 18–22 minutes (this includes unpin + reverse rollout + cache invalidation + validation sweep). We’ll include the node snapshot restore steps in the runbook so you can trace timing.
- Audit & retention: yes — we will publish a signed runbook snapshot (PDF) and the orchestration event log. Redwood will retain the operation logs in the audit bundle for 90 days and provide a checksum and signed manifest.
- Fallback behavior: the warm fallback variant is functionally equivalent for inference features; it is a lower-performance build (reduced batching aggressiveness and smaller KV prefetch window) but should preserve feature parity (no function/tool-calling or structured-output regressions). Any edge-case capability differences will be noted in the runbook.

Action items before the window (owners):
- Karthik: add BGP adjacency stabilisation gate + explicit convergence wait and a metrics export step (Karthik will attach the metrics snapshot).
- Monica: prepare the signed runbook snapshot and orchestration event log retention path.
- Soojin: validate fallback variant behavior with a lightweight smoke test (no model diff expected) and note any feature flags.
- Stephanie: final runbook update and send a short post-mortem template that we’ll use in case of rollback.

I’ll update the runbook and send the final version by EOD tomorrow. If anything changes on your side, flag immediately.

Thanks —
Stephanie Nguyen
Sr. Platform PM, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: updated_runbook_v1.1.pdf (will be attached in follow-up)
